title_en: Amendment (IV) to the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 145 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: “Whoever produces medical instruments or medical sanitary materials that do not conform to the national or industrial standards for ensuring human health, or sells such medical instruments or medical sanitary materials knowing that they do not conform to the national or industrial standards for ensuring human health, if such conduct is sufficient to seriously endanger human health, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and shall also be fined not less than 50 percent but not more than two times the sales amount; if serious harm is caused to human health, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and shall also be fined not less than 50 percent but not more than two times the sales amount; if the consequences are especially serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and shall also be fined not less than 50 percent but not more than two times the sales amount, or shall have property confiscated.”

A paragraph is added to Article 152 as paragraph 2: “Whoever evades customs supervision to transport solid waste, liquid waste, or gaseous waste from outside the territory into the territory, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years and shall also be fined, or be fined only; if the circumstances are especially serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years and shall also be fined.”
The original paragraph 2 is amended as paragraph 3 to read: “Where a unit commits the crime prescribed in the preceding two paragraphs, the unit shall be fined, and the person directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs.”

Article 155 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: “The following acts shall be dealt with as smuggling crimes and punished according to the relevant provisions of this Section: (1) directly and illegally purchasing from smugglers articles the import of which is prohibited by the State, or directly and illegally purchasing from smugglers other goods or articles smuggled into the country, if the value involved is relatively large; (2) transporting, purchasing, or selling in the inland sea, territorial waters, boundary rivers, or boundary lakes articles the import or export of which is prohibited by the State, or transporting, purchasing, or selling goods or articles the import or export of which is restricted by the State, if the value involved is relatively large and without lawful certificates.”

Article 244a is added after Article 244 of the Criminal Law: “Whoever, in violation of labor management regulations, employs minors under the age of 16 to engage in ultra-intensive physical labor, or to engage in high-altitude or underground operations, or to work in explosive, inflammable, radioactive, toxic, or other dangerous environments, if the circumstances are serious, the person directly responsible shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention and shall also be fined; if the circumstances are especially serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and shall also be fined.
“Where an act prescribed in the preceding paragraph causes an accident and also constitutes another crime, the offender shall be punished in accordance with the provisions on combined punishment for multiple crimes.”

Article 339, paragraph 3 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: “Whoever, under the pretext of using as raw materials, imports solid waste, liquid waste, or gaseous waste that cannot be used as raw materials shall be convicted and punished according to the provisions of Article 152, paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Law.”

Article 344 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: “Whoever, in violation of State regulations, illegally fells or destroys precious trees or other plants under special State protection, or illegally purchases, transports, processes, or sells precious trees or other plants under special State protection or the products thereof, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance and shall also be fined; if the circumstances are serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and shall also be fined.”

Article 345 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: “Whoever illegally fells forests or other woods, if the quantity is relatively large, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and shall also be fined, or be fined only; if the quantity is huge, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and shall also be fined; if the quantity is especially huge, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than seven years and shall also be fined.
“Whoever, in violation of the provisions of the Forest Law, indiscriminately fells forests or other woods, if the quantity is relatively large, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and shall also be fined, or be fined only; if the quantity is huge, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and shall also be fined.
“Whoever illegally purchases or transports trees or woods knowingly felled or indiscriminately felled, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and shall also be fined, or be fined only; if the circumstances are especially serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and shall also be fined.
“Whoever illegally fells or indiscriminately fells forests or other woods in a national nature reserve shall be given a severe punishment.”

Article 399 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: “Any judicial officer who, for the purpose of favoring a friend or engaging in malpractice for personal gain, knowingly subjects a person who is obviously innocent to prosecution, intentionally shields a person who is obviously guilty from prosecution, or intentionally perverts the law in rendering a judgment in criminal adjudication activities, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if the circumstances are serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years; if the circumstances are especially serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years.
“Whoever intentionally perverts the law in rendering a judgment in civil or administrative adjudication activities, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if the circumstances are especially serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years.
“In the enforcement of judgments or rulings, whoever is seriously irresponsible or abuses his power, fails to take preservation measures according to law, fails to perform statutory enforcement duties, or illegally takes preservation measures or compulsory execution measures, thereby causing major losses to the interests of the party or others, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if especially major losses are caused to the interests of the party or others, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years.
“Where a judicial officer accepts bribes and commits any of the acts prescribed in the preceding three paragraphs, and such act also constitutes a crime as prescribed in Article 385 of this Law, the offender shall be convicted and punished according to the provisions for a heavier punishment.”
This Amendment shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
